scope: the biggest gap of the whole campaign was in the distribution channel, not in a checker

finding.what: site/plugins.json — the market index a user actually adds as a source — listed 9 plugins while 28 were published
finding.impact: 19 published packages could not be installed from the index at all, and the 9 that could were pinned to hard-coded versions that had already moved on
finding.rootCause: scripts/build-market-index.mjs carried a hand-written KITS array of 8 entries with literal version strings, and asserted `validated.plugins.length !== 9` against another literal
sameMistakeThreeTimes: the count assertion in the script
finding.whyMissed: every round verified the upstream catalog (catalog-coverage, PR gates, feed) and never the index this project publishes itself. The distribution layer was assumed, not checked.

fix.derived: KITS is now built from the two kit repositories: checks-data.mjs for slug/title/description, package.json for the published version
fix.counts: the expected count is 1 + KITS.length, and the home page counts check packages from the published index instead of a literal
fix.gate: test/market-index-coverage.test.js asserts every published package is in the index, every indexed version matches its package.json, and the build script carries no literal plugin count

verified.homePage: 27 check packages, 5 verification, 22 industry — all derived

feedPrediction.result: probe had not run yet; feed still 26 of mine
feedPrediction.status: prediction stands, verification due after 02:23 UTC

lesson: the same hand-maintained-list pattern had already cost four site-build test failures this week; this is the same pattern one layer out, where the cost was that two thirds of the catalogue was unreachable rather than a red test.
